chart.title: Eastbrook in 1995 and 2020

text: The two maps illustrate how the village of Eastbrook changed between 1995 and 2020.

Overall, the village became considerably more developed over the period. Farmland disappeared and was replaced by housing, while the local shop gave way to a much larger supermarket, and facilities for both education and transport were improved.

In 1995, the north-west of the village was occupied by farmland, with a small school to the north-east. South of the Main Road stood a shop, a group of houses and a church, and the river had no crossing. By 2020, the farmland had been completely replaced by a new housing estate. The Main Road ran across the centre of the village.

The school had been enlarged, and a sports field had been added next to it. The shop had been demolished and replaced by a supermarket with its own car park, whereas the existing houses and church were left unchanged. In addition, a new bridge had been built across the river, which improved access to the south of the village. The road itself was not altered.
